headline: Brazil Votes in Runoff Between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro
dek: Final polls put the incumbent and the senator Trump has praised within the margin of error.
brief: Lula, 80, seeks a fourth term against Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, 45, whose father is serving 27 years over a plot to overturn the 2022 election. Flávio led the first round 47% to 45%.

framing.left: Lula and the Workers' Party call Flávio “dangerous” and cast the vote as a stand against U.S. interference in Brazil.
framing.right: Flávio and the Liberal Party say “Brazil needs change,” promising a crackdown on gangs and better deals with Washington.

reading.label: The Stakes
reading.text: One camp speaks of “interference,” the other of “change”; the contest beneath is over the presidency, the courts, and Brazil's tilt between Washington and Beijing.

context: 2022: Lula defeats Jair Bolsonaro by under two points
4 Oct 2026: Flávio 47%, Lula 45% in the first round
